# System Qualification Test Specification (SYS.5)
## HVAC Flap Actuator Prototype
## ASPICE SYS.5 – End-to-End System Test Plan

## 1. Scope and Purpose
This test specification defines the **System Qualification Test Cases** required to validate the HVAC Flap Actuator system in an integrated, hardware bench environment. It covers *full system behavior*, validating compliance to customer/system requirements only through observable, externally verifiable results. Unit/integration/internal/RTOS/diagnostics/cybersecurity are out of scope.

**Coverage:**
- All externally observable system behaviors per SYS-REQ-001 ... SYS-REQ-038
- Power-up, initialization, actuation sequence, feedback, indicator LEDs, error and boundary conditions
- UART (user command), ADC (position feedback), GPIO/PWM (motor control), and LED indication


## 2. Test Environment
- Full hardware bench setup with production-representative actuator, motor, feedback potentiometer, LEDs, and standard UART interface via PC
- Power supply and ability to simulate power-cycles
- Human/user command source (UART terminal)

## 4. Detailed Test Case Descriptions

### 4.1 SYS-TC-001: Power-Up & Initialization
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-019, SYS-REQ-020, SYS-REQ-021, SYS-REQ-017
- **Test Objective:** Verify correct peripheral initialization, motor OFF state, and initial flap position detection with LED indication upon system power-up.
- **Preconditions:** System powered OFF and configured per bench setup.
- **Test Inputs:** Power ON (supply toggle).
- **Test Steps:**
  1. Power ON the system hardware.
  2. Observe all status and position LEDs.
  3. Record motor state (should remain OFF).
  4. Confirm correct startup LED status and initial flap position LED.
- **Expected Results:**
  - Power/status LED turns ON.
  - System initializes peripherals (by observation, e.g., no error state, system responsive).
  - Motor remains OFF.
  - One position LED turns ON, indicating flap position.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** All expected results observed. No unintended behaviors (e.g., motor jerk, multiple LEDs ON).

### 4.2 SYS-TC-002: Valid Flap Position Commands (Nominal)
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-002, SYS-REQ-003, SYS-REQ-004, SYS-REQ-007, SYS-REQ-008, SYS-REQ-009, SYS-REQ-013, SYS-REQ-016, SYS-REQ-018
- **Test Objective:** Confirm the system moves the flap actuator to all supported positions (0–5) on valid UART command, with correct motor control and LED position feedback.
- **Preconditions:** System powered ON, initialized, idle, with flap at any position.
- **Test Inputs:** UART commands for positions 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (sequentially).
- **Test Steps:**
  1. For each position X (0–5):
      a. Send UART command 'X'.
      b. Observe motor starts and runs only as long as required.
      c. Observe flap moves to requested position (physically or via feedback/indicator).
      d. Confirm motor stops at target.
      e. Confirm only one corresponding position LED is ON.
- **Expected Results:**
  - Flap moves to commanded position.
  - Motor starts/stops correctly; no overshoot.
  - One corresponding position LED ON per command.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** Flap reaches commanded position with no overshoot/undershoot; motor stops; LEDs indicate correct position.

### 4.3 SYS-TC-003: Invalid & Boundary Condition Handling
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-005, SYS-REQ-014, SYS-REQ-012, SYS-REQ-023, SYS-REQ-034
- **Test Objective:** Validate the system safely ignores/handles out-of-range/invalid UART commands and ADC values, and commands during movement.
- **Preconditions:** System powered ON and idle.
- **Test Inputs:** UART commands (-1, 6, 255, ASCII letters etc.), simultaneous UART command during flap movement, synthetic ADC input out-of-bounds (hardware assist if possible).
- **Test Steps:**
  1. Send invalid UART commands (e.g., -1, 6, 'A').
  2. During a valid move, inject a new UART command.
  3. Simulate/force an invalid ADC feedback value (if hardware permits).
  4. Monitor system for resets, lockups, or error indications.
- **Expected Results:**
  - System ignores invalid inputs (no action, no erroneous output).
  - No reset or lock-up occurs.
  - On invalid ADC: motor stops, no erratic movement, and system remains stable.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** No actuation, no error LED, system responsive/idle after invalid input.

### 4.4 SYS-TC-004: Position Feedback & Monitoring
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-010, SYS-REQ-011, SYS-REQ-021, SYS-REQ-023
- **Test Objective:** Confirm ADC readings correctly map to valid flap positions, system monitors feedback continuously, and ignores ADC out-of-range values.
- **Preconditions:** System powered ON.
- **Test Inputs:** Adjust flap potentiometer across entire range (if accessible), or command movements to cover all positions; inject out-of-range ADC if possible.
- **Test Steps:**
  1. Move flap to each valid position; note ADC mapped to 0-5 only.
  2. Manually/electronically set/force ADC to out-of-range value.
  3. Observe system and LED behavior.
- **Expected Results:**
  - Every physical position only lights the corresponding position LED.
  - Out-of-range ADC values are ignored, no movement induced.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** Correct LED only for valid ADC; no action for invalid ADC. System stays stable/idle.

### 4.5 SYS-TC-005: Motor Control Behavior
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-006, SYS-REQ-007, SYS-REQ-008, SYS-REQ-009, SYS-REQ-034
- **Test Objective:** Validate correct start, stop, and direction control of the motor.
- **Preconditions:** System ON, idle, flap at any position.
- **Test Inputs:** UART position commands (0–5, various orders).
- **Test Steps:**
  1. Send command to move flap from one extreme (0) to the other (5), and vice versa.
  2. Observe initial motor direction and actuation.
  3. Interrupt movement with valid/invalid command and observe effect.
  4. At end-of-travel or command completion, assess if motor OFF.
- **Expected Results:**
  - Motor runs in correct direction to commanded position.
  - Motor stops *promptly* at target.
  - No unintended movement post-arrival.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** Only expected motor activity (no drift/noise post-move). No uncontrolled movement.

### 4.6 SYS-TC-006: LED Status Indication
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-016, SYS-REQ-017, SYS-REQ-018, SYS-REQ-020
- **Test Objective:** Ensure correct operation of power and position LEDs through all modes.
- **Preconditions:** System ON.
- **Test Inputs:** Power cycle, UART commands for all positions.
- **Test Steps:**
  1. Observe LEDs upon power-up and during each movement.
  2. Send commands to each position (0–5) and note LED pattern.
- **Expected Results:**
  - Power/status LED ON when powered.
  - Only one position LED ON at any time.
  - Correct LED changes for each position/move.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** LED outputs match specification in every state.

### 4.7 SYS-TC-007: End-to-End System Sequence
- **Mapped System Requirement ID(s):** SYS-REQ-001, SYS-REQ-002, SYS-REQ-003, SYS-REQ-004, SYS-REQ-007, SYS-REQ-010, SYS-REQ-016, SYS-REQ-017, SYS-REQ-018, SYS-REQ-021, SYS-REQ-038
- **Test Objective:** Validate complete sequence: user command input to actuator operation, correct feedback, and visual indication. Demonstrates correct system integration.
- **Preconditions:** Power cycle system to initialize, then send representative commands.
- **Test Inputs:** Power ON, UART command any valid/invalid order.
- **Test Steps:**
  1. Power up; confirm system initializes.
  2. Issue valid position command (UART); observe flap moves, feedback accepted, LEDs correctly update.
  3. Issue invalid command (UART or ADC); observe no action, no error LED.
  4. Repeat with mix of edge/boundary values.
- **Expected Results:**
  - User commands induce correct actuator response.
  - Feedback and LEDs always consistent and correct.
  - System is resilient to invalid/erroneous input.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** All expected behaviors seen end-to-end as per requirements.
